name: middleware
description: Composable HTTP handler wrappers: CORS, security headers and CSP, request ids, access logs, limits, deadlines, negotiation, auth and host checks

api.name: header_in
api.sig: fn header_in(hs: List[(Str, Str)], name: Str) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc: The first value of the header `name` in `hs`, matched case-insensitively.

api.name: header_values
api.sig: fn header_values(hs: List[(Str, Str)], name: Str) -> List[Str]
api.doc: Every value of the header `name` in `hs`, in order, matched case-insensitively.

api.name: valid_header_name
api.sig: fn valid_header_name(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `s` is a field name (an RFC 9110 token: letters, digits and ``!#$%&'*+-.^_`|~``).

api.name: valid_header_value
api.sig: fn valid_header_value(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `s` can be sent as a field value: no CR, LF or NUL, so it can't split the response.

api.name: set_header
api.sig: fn set_header(r: Response, name: Str, value: Str) -> Response
api.doc: `r` with the header `name` set to `value`, replacing every earlier value of it.

api.name: add_header
api.sig: fn add_header(r: Response, name: Str, value: Str) -> Response
api.doc: `r` with one more `name: value` header, keeping the values it has (for `set-cookie` and `link`).

api.name: remove_header
api.sig: fn remove_header(r: Response, name: Str) -> Response
api.doc: `r` without any header called `name`.

api.name: default_header
api.sig: fn default_header(r: Response, name: Str, value: Str) -> Response
api.doc: `r` with `name: value` unless it already has a header called `name`.

api.name: set_request_header
api.sig: fn set_request_header(req: Request, name: Str, value: Str) -> Request
api.doc: `req` with the header `name` set to `value`, replacing every earlier value of it.

api.name: remove_request_header
api.sig: fn remove_request_header(req: Request, name: Str) -> Request
api.doc: `req` without any header called `name`.

api.name: split_list
api.sig: fn split_list(s: Str) -> List[Str]
api.doc: The elements of a comma-separated field value, trimmed, without empty ones (RFC 9110 5.6.1).

api.name: add_vary
api.sig: fn add_vary(r: Response, field: Str) -> Response
api.doc: `r` with `field` in its `Vary` header, merged with what is there; `Vary: *` is left alone.

api.name: reason_phrase
api.sig: fn reason_phrase(status: Int) -> Str
api.doc: The reason phrase of a status code from RFC 9110 and its companions, or "" for an unknown one.

api.name: problem
api.sig: fn problem(status: Int where _ >= 400 and _ <= 599, detail: Str) -> Response
api.doc:
An RFC 9457 problem details response (`application/problem+json`) with type `about:blank`,
the status's reason phrase as its title and `detail` (left out when empty).

api.name: problem_with
api.sig: fn problem_with(status: Int where _ >= 400 and _ <= 599, detail: Str, members: List[(Str, Str)]) -> Response
api.doc:
A problem details response like `problem`, with extension members: each pair is a member name
and its value, already encoded as JSON (`json.encode(x)`).

api.name: redirect
api.sig: fn redirect(status: Int where _ == 301 or _ == 302 or _ == 303 or _ == 307 or _ == 308, location: Str) -> Response
api.doc: A redirect to `location` with `status` (301, 302, 303, 307 or 308) and an empty body.

api.name: compose
api.sig: fn compose[e](layers: List[(Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e], h: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e
api.doc:
The handler `h` inside `layers`, the first layer outermost: `compose([a, b], h)` is `a(b(h))`.
Every layer must keep the effect row as it is (cors, secure, limits, guards); nest wrappers that
add `log`, `time` or `rand` directly around the result, `request_ids(p, compose([...], h))`.

api.name: only_when
api.sig: fn only_when[e](pred: Request -> Bool, layer: (Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e, next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e
api.doc:
`layer` around `next` for requests that satisfy `pred`; others go straight to `next`. The layer
keeps the effect row, as for `compose`.

api.name: under
api.sig: fn under(prefix: Str, req: Request) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether the path of `req` is `prefix` or below it (`/api` covers `/api` and `/api/x`, not `/apix`).

api.name: before
api.sig: fn before[e](f: Request -> Request, next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e
api.doc: A wrapper that changes the request before `next` sees it.

api.name: after
api.sig: fn after[e](f: (Request, Response) -> Response, next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e
api.doc: A wrapper that changes the response `next` gives, seeing the request too.

api.name: with_headers
api.sig: fn with_headers[e](hs: List[(Str, Str)], next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e
api.doc:
A wrapper that sets each of `hs` on every response (for example a fixed `server` header),
replacing the handler's values.

api.name: strip_headers
api.sig: fn strip_headers[e](names: List[Str], next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e
api.doc: A wrapper that removes the headers called `names` from every response (`x-powered-by`, `server`).

api.name: no_store
api.sig: fn no_store[e](next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e
api.doc: A wrapper that marks responses `cache-control: no-store` unless the handler set `cache-control`.

api.name: percent_decode
api.sig: fn percent_decode(s: Str, plus: Bool) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc:
`s` with `%XX` escapes decoded, and `+` as a space when `plus` is true (form encoding). `none`
for a truncated or non-hex escape, or bytes that are not UTF-8.

api.name: percent_encode
api.sig: fn percent_encode(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
`s` percent-encoded for a URL component: every byte except the RFC 3986 unreserved characters
(letters, digits, `-`, `.`, `_`, `~`) becomes `%XX`.

api.name: query_string
api.sig: fn query_string(url: Str) -> Str
api.doc: The query string of a request target, without the `?`, or "".

api.name: query_pairs
api.sig: fn query_pairs(url: Str) -> List[(Str, Str)]
api.doc:
The decoded `name=value` pairs of a request target's query string, in order. A pair without `=`
has the value ""; a pair that does not decode is kept as it was sent.

api.name: redact_query
api.sig: fn redact_query(url: Str, names: List[Str]) -> Str
api.doc:
The request target `url` with the values of the query parameters called `names` (compared
case-insensitively) replaced by `REDACTED`, for logs.

api.name: Weighted
api.sig: pub type Weighted = {value: Str, params: List[(Str, Str)], q: F64} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
One element of an `Accept`-style field: its value, its parameters (lowercased names) and its
weight from `q`, 1.0 when absent.

api.name: parse_weighted
api.sig: fn parse_weighted(header: Str) -> List[Weighted]
api.doc:
The elements of an `Accept`, `Accept-Encoding`, `Accept-Language` or `Accept-Charset` value in
the order sent. Elements with a malformed or repeated `q` are dropped (RFC 9110 12.4.2).

api.name: negotiate_media
api.sig: fn negotiate_media(header: Str, offers: List[Str]) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc:
The offer (a media type, possibly with parameters) that best fits the `Accept` value `header`:
the most specific matching range gives each offer its weight, the highest weight wins and ties
go to the earlier offer. An empty header accepts the first offer; `none` means 406.

api.name: negotiate_encoding
api.sig: fn negotiate_encoding(header: Str, offers: List[Str]) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc:
The content coding to use for the `Accept-Encoding` value `header` among `offers` (RFC 9110
12.5.3): `x-gzip` is `gzip`, `*` covers unlisted codings, and `identity` is acceptable unless
excluded. A missing header (pass "") prefers `identity` when offered. `none` means nothing offered
is acceptable.

api.name: negotiate_language
api.sig: fn negotiate_language(header: Str, offers: List[Str]) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc:
The language tag among `offers` that best fits the `Accept-Language` value `header`, by RFC 4647
basic filtering: `en` matches `en` and `en-GB`, `*` matches anything, the longest matching range
gives the weight, and ties go to the earlier offer. An empty header picks the first offer.

api.name: media_type
api.sig: fn media_type(content_type: Str) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc:
The media type of a `Content-Type` value, lowercased, without parameters: `type/subtype`, or
`none` when it has no `/`.

api.name: media_matches
api.sig: fn media_matches(pattern: Str, mt: Str) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether the media type `mt` matches `pattern`: an exact type, `type/*`, `*/*`, or a structured
suffix such as `application/*+json`.

api.name: Cors
api.sig: pub type Cors = {origins: List[Str] where _.all(valid_origin_pattern), any_origin: Bool, methods: List[Str] where _.all(valid_header_name), allow_headers: List[Str] where _.all(valid_header_name), any_header: Bool, expose_headers: List[Str] where _.all(valid_header_name), credentials: Bool, max_age_s: Int where _ >= -1 and _ <= 86400, private_network: Bool} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A CORS policy (the Fetch standard's CORS protocol). `origins` are exact origins
(`https://app.example.com`, `http://localhost:3000`), wildcard subdomains
(`https://*.example.com`, which does not match `example.com` itself) or `null`, which must be
listed to be allowed. `any_origin` allows every origin and can't be combined with
`credentials`. `methods` and `allow_headers` are what preflights may ask for (`any_header`
allows any header), `expose_headers` what scripts may read, `max_age_s` how long a browser may
cache a preflight (-1 sends no `Access-Control-Max-Age`), and `private_network` answers Private
Network Access preflights.

api.name: cors_for
api.sig: fn cors_for(origins: List[Str]) -> Cors
api.doc:
A policy for `origins` without credentials: the methods GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH and
DELETE, the request headers `content-type`, `authorization` and `x-requested-with`, nothing
exposed, and preflights cached for 10 minutes.

api.name: cors_public
api.sig: fn cors_public() -> Cors
api.doc: A policy that lets any origin read responses without credentials, for public APIs.

api.name: valid_origin_pattern
api.sig: fn valid_origin_pattern(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether `s` is a valid entry of `Cors.origins`: `null`, or `scheme://host[:port]` where the host
may start with `*.`, with no path, query, fragment or user info.

api.name: origin_matches
api.sig: fn origin_matches(pattern: Str, origin: Str) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether the `Origin` value `origin` matches the pattern `pattern` (see `Cors`). Schemes and hosts
compare case-insensitively and default ports are the same as none.

api.name: cors_allows
api.sig: fn cors_allows(p: Cors, origin: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `p` lets the origin `origin` read responses.

api.name: is_preflight
api.sig: fn is_preflight(req: Request) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `req` is a CORS preflight: `OPTIONS` with `Origin` and `Access-Control-Request-Method`.

api.name: cors_preflight
api.sig: fn cors_preflight(p: Cors, req: Request) -> Response
api.doc:
The answer to the preflight `req` under `p`: `204` with the `Access-Control-Allow-*` headers when
the origin, the method and every requested header are allowed, otherwise `403` without them, so
the browser blocks the request. Either way it varies on the request's CORS headers.

api.name: cors_headers
api.sig: fn cors_headers(p: Cors, req: Request) -> List[(Str, Str)]
api.doc:
The CORS headers for the response to the non-preflight request `req` under `p`: the allowed
origin (or `*` for a public policy), credentials and exposed headers when the origin is allowed,
and `Vary: Origin` whenever the answer depends on it.

api.name: cors
api.sig: fn cors[e](p: Cors, next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e
api.doc:
A wrapper that answers preflights itself and adds CORS headers to the other responses of `next`.
Use it instead of the `Server.cors` field when you need credentials, wildcard subdomains,
exposed headers or per-route policies.

api.name: Hsts
api.sig: pub type Hsts = {max_age_s: Int where _ >= 0, include_subdomains: Bool, preload: Bool} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
`Strict-Transport-Security` (RFC 6797). Preloading needs a max age of at least a year and
`include_subdomains`.

api.name: hsts_value
api.sig: fn hsts_value(h: Hsts) -> Str
api.doc: The `Strict-Transport-Security` value for `h`.

api.name: Csp
api.sig: pub type Csp = {directives: List[(Str, List[Str])], report_only: Bool} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A Content Security Policy (CSP Level 3): directives in order, each with its sources, sent as
`Content-Security-Policy`, or `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` when `report_only`.

api.name: valid_directive
api.sig: fn valid_directive(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `s` is a CSP directive name: lowercase letters and `-`.

api.name: valid_source
api.sig: fn valid_source(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether `s` can be a CSP source expression: printable, without whitespace, `;` or `,`, which
would end the directive or the policy.

api.name: csp_empty
api.sig: fn csp_empty() -> Csp
api.doc: An empty policy.

api.name: csp_strict
api.sig: fn csp_strict() -> Csp
api.doc:
A strict starting policy: `default-src 'self'`, `base-uri 'none'`, `object-src 'none'`,
`frame-ancestors 'none'`, `form-action 'self'`.

api.name: csp_helmet
api.sig: fn csp_helmet() -> Csp
api.doc:
The policy helmet sends by default: `default-src 'self'`, `base-uri 'self'`, `font-src 'self'
https: data:`, `form-action 'self'`, `frame-ancestors 'self'`, `img-src 'self' data:`,
`object-src 'none'`, `script-src 'self'`, `script-src-attr 'none'`, `style-src 'self' https:
'unsafe-inline'`, `upgrade-insecure-requests`.

api.name: csp_set
api.sig: fn csp_set(c: Csp, name: Str, sources: List[Str]) -> Csp
api.doc:
`c` with the directive `name` set to `sources`, replacing it if present (a directive with no
sources, such as `upgrade-insecure-requests`, is written as its name alone).

api.name: csp_add
api.sig: fn csp_add(c: Csp, name: Str, sources: List[Str]) -> Csp
api.doc:
`c` with `sources` added to the directive `name` (created when missing), without duplicates.
A directive that only had `'none'` loses it.

api.name: csp_remove
api.sig: fn csp_remove(c: Csp, name: Str) -> Csp
api.doc: `c` without the directive `name`.

api.name: csp_report_only
api.sig: fn csp_report_only(c: Csp, on: Bool) -> Csp
api.doc: `c` sent in report-only mode (or enforced when `on` is false).

api.name: csp_value
api.sig: fn csp_value(c: Csp) -> Str
api.doc: The policy text of `c`: directives separated by `; `.

api.name: csp_header
api.sig: fn csp_header(c: Csp) -> (Str, Str)
api.doc: The header for `c`: its name (enforcing or report-only) and value.

api.name: src_self
api.sig: fn src_self() -> Str
api.doc: The source `'self'`.

api.name: src_none
api.sig: fn src_none() -> Str
api.doc: The source `'none'`.

api.name: src_unsafe_inline
api.sig: fn src_unsafe_inline() -> Str
api.doc: The source `'unsafe-inline'`.

api.name: src_unsafe_eval
api.sig: fn src_unsafe_eval() -> Str
api.doc: The source `'unsafe-eval'`.

api.name: src_wasm_unsafe_eval
api.sig: fn src_wasm_unsafe_eval() -> Str
api.doc: The source `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.

api.name: src_strict_dynamic
api.sig: fn src_strict_dynamic() -> Str
api.doc: The source `'strict-dynamic'`.

api.name: src_report_sample
api.sig: fn src_report_sample() -> Str
api.doc: The source `'report-sample'`.

api.name: src_nonce
api.sig: fn src_nonce(nonce: Str where _.len > 0 and _.chars.all(c => c.is_alpha or "0123456789+/-_=".contains(c))) -> Str
api.doc: The source `'nonce-<nonce>'`; `nonce` must be base64 or base64url text.

api.name: src_sha256
api.sig: fn src_sha256(content: Str) -> Str
api.doc: The source `'sha256-<base64>'` that allows the inline script or style `content` exactly.

api.name: src_sha512
api.sig: fn src_sha512(content: Str) -> Str
api.doc: The source `'sha512-<base64>'` that allows the inline script or style `content` exactly.

api.name: permissions_policy
api.sig: fn permissions_policy(features: List[(Str, List[Str])]) -> Str
api.doc:
A `Permissions-Policy` value (a structured field dictionary): each feature with its allowlist,
where `self` and `src` are keywords, `*` allows every origin and other entries are origins.
An empty allowlist disables the feature.

api.name: Security
api.sig: pub type Security = {hsts: Opt[Hsts], csp: Opt[Csp], frame: Str where _.frame_ok, referrer: Str where _.referrer_ok, nosniff: Bool, coop: Str where _.coop_ok, coep: Str where _.coep_ok, corp: Str where _.corp_ok, permissions: Str where valid_header_value(_), dns_prefetch: Str where _.onoff_ok, cross_domain: Str where _.xdomain_ok, origin_agent_cluster: Bool, xss_off: Bool, overwrite: Bool} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
The security headers to send, after OWASP's HTTP Headers Cheat Sheet and helmet. A field that
is `none` or "" sends nothing: `frame` is `X-Frame-Options` (`DENY` or `SAMEORIGIN`),
`referrer` is `Referrer-Policy`, `coop`, `coep` and `corp` are the `Cross-Origin-*-Policy`
headers, `permissions` is a `permissions_policy` value, `dns_prefetch` is
`X-DNS-Prefetch-Control`, `cross_domain` is `X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies`. `nosniff` sends
`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `origin_agent_cluster` sends `Origin-Agent-Cluster: ?1`, and
`xss_off` sends `X-XSS-Protection: 0`, which turns off the legacy filter that caused leaks.
With `overwrite` false, headers the handler set are kept.

api.name: security_defaults
api.sig: fn security_defaults() -> Security
api.doc:
helmet's defaults: `csp_helmet`, HSTS for a year with subdomains, `SAMEORIGIN` framing,
`no-referrer`, nosniff, COOP and CORP `same-origin`, no COEP, DNS prefetching off, no
cross-domain policies, `Origin-Agent-Cluster`, the XSS filter off, and handler headers kept.

api.name: security_api
api.sig: fn security_api() -> Security
api.doc:
Defaults for a JSON API that no browser should render or frame: `csp_strict` with
`default-src 'none'`, `DENY`, `no-referrer`, nosniff, CORP `same-origin`, HSTS for a year.

api.name: security_headers
api.sig: fn security_headers(s: Security) -> List[(Str, Str)]
api.doc: The headers `s` sends, in a fixed order.

api.name: apply_security
api.sig: fn apply_security(s: Security, r: Response) -> Response
api.doc:
`r` with the headers of `s`: replacing the handler's when `s.overwrite`, otherwise only where
the handler set none.

api.name: secure
api.sig: fn secure[e](s: Security, next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e
api.doc:
A wrapper that adds the security headers of `s` to every response of `next`. HSTS only takes
effect over HTTPS; behind a TLS-terminating proxy that is the browser's connection, so it is
sent regardless.

api.name: nonce_header
api.sig: fn nonce_header() -> Str
api.doc: The request header that carries the per-request CSP nonce to the handler.

api.name: request_nonce
api.sig: fn request_nonce(req: Request) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc: The CSP nonce `with_nonce` gave this request, for `<script nonce="...">` in the page.

api.name: with_nonce
api.sig: fn with_nonce[e](c: Csp, next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e, rand
api.doc:
A wrapper that makes a fresh 128-bit nonce for each request, passes it to `next` in the
`x-csp-nonce` request header (any such header from the client is replaced), and sends `c` with
`'nonce-...'` added to `script-src` and `style-src`.

api.name: RequestIds
api.sig: pub type RequestIds = {header: Str where valid_header_name(_), trust_incoming: Bool, max_len: Int where _ >= 8 and _ <= 200} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
How request ids are handled: the header that carries them in both directions, whether an id
the client sent is kept, and the longest one accepted.

api.name: request_ids_default
api.sig: fn request_ids_default() -> RequestIds
api.doc: `x-request-id`, client ids kept when valid, up to 128 characters.

api.name: valid_request_id
api.sig: fn valid_request_id(id: Str, max_len: Int) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether `id` is an acceptable request id: 1 to `max_len` characters from letters, digits and
`-_.:`, so it is safe to log and to echo.

api.name: request_id
api.sig: fn request_id(req: Request) -> Str
api.doc: The request id of `req` under `http.serve`, which always sets `x-request-id`, or "".

api.name: request_ids
api.sig: fn request_ids[e](p: RequestIds, next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e, rand, time
api.doc:
A wrapper that gives each request an id in `p.header`: the client's when trusted and valid,
otherwise a fresh UUIDv7, and echoes it on the response.

api.name: AccessEntry
api.sig: pub type AccessEntry = {method: Str, target: Str, status: Int, ms: Int, size: Int, id: Str, agent: Str, referer: Str} derive Eq, Show, Json
api.doc:
One access log line: method, path with the query (secrets redacted), status, milliseconds,
response body bytes, request id, user agent and referrer.

api.name: AccessLog
api.sig: pub type AccessLog = {skip: List[Str], redact: List[Str], slow_ms: Int where _ >= 0} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
What the access log writes: paths not to log (`/healthz`, matched like `under`), query parameters
to redact, and the time from which a line is a warning (0 never). 5xx answers are errors and
4xx answers are warnings.

api.name: access_log_default
api.sig: fn access_log_default() -> AccessLog
api.doc:
No skipped paths; `token`, `code`, `password`, `secret`, `key` and `signature` redacted; slow
from 1 second.

api.name: access_entry
api.sig: fn access_entry(p: AccessLog, req: Request, r: Response, ms: Int) -> AccessEntry
api.doc: The entry for `req` answered with `r` in `ms` milliseconds.

api.name: access_level
api.sig: fn access_level(p: AccessLog, a: AccessEntry) -> Str
api.doc: The level an entry is logged at: `error` for 5xx, `warn` for 4xx or slow answers, else `info`.

api.name: access_log
api.sig: fn access_log[e](p: AccessLog, next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e, log, time
api.doc:
A wrapper that times `next` on the monotonic clock and logs one JSON line per request through
`log.info`, `log.warn` or `log.error`, so `SSPUR_LOG=json` gives its fields as the line's fields.
Turn off the server's own `access_log` to avoid two lines.

api.name: server_timing
api.sig: fn server_timing[e](next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e, time
api.doc:
A wrapper that reports the handler's time on the monotonic clock in `Server-Timing` (`app;dur=`
milliseconds with one decimal), which browsers show in their developer tools. Only use it where
timings may be public.

api.name: content_length
api.sig: fn content_length(req: Request) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
The `Content-Length` of `req`: `some(n)` when present and a valid decimal number, `some(-1)`
when present and invalid, `none` when absent.

api.name: body_problem
api.sig: fn body_problem(req: Request, max: Int where _ >= 0) -> Opt[Response]
api.doc:
The error response for a body over `max` bytes (`413`), or a malformed `Content-Length`
(`400`), or `none` when the body is acceptable.

api.name: body_limit
api.sig: fn body_limit[e](max: Int where _ >= 0, next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e
api.doc:
A wrapper that answers `413` for bodies over `max` bytes, for routes that need less than the
server's `max_body`.

api.name: media_problem
api.sig: fn media_problem(req: Request, types: List[Str]) -> Opt[Response]
api.doc:
The `415` response for a `POST`, `PUT` or `PATCH` request with a body whose media type matches
none of `types` (patterns as in `media_matches`), with `Accept-Post` or `Accept-Patch` naming
them; `none` when the request is acceptable.

api.name: require_media
api.sig: fn require_media[e](types: List[Str], next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e
api.doc: A wrapper that answers `415` unless request bodies are of one of `types`.

api.name: Deadline
api.sig: pub type Deadline = {ms: Int where _ > 0, header: Str where valid_header_name(_), replace_late: Bool} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A time budget per request: `ms` milliseconds, announced to the handler in the request header
`header` as the absolute deadline in Unix milliseconds. With `replace_late`, a response that
comes after the deadline is replaced by `503` (only for GET, HEAD and OPTIONS, since other
methods may have changed something).

api.name: deadline_of
api.sig: fn deadline_of(ms: Int where _ > 0) -> Deadline
api.doc: `ms` milliseconds in `x-request-deadline`, late safe responses replaced.

api.name: remaining_ms
api.sig: fn remaining_ms(req: Request, header: Str, now_ms: Int) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
The milliseconds left at `now_ms` before the deadline in `header`, at least 0, or `none` when the
request has no deadline. Pass it on as the `timeout_ms` of outgoing calls.

api.name: deadline
api.sig: fn deadline[e](d: Deadline, next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e, time
api.doc:
A wrapper that sets the deadline header (replacing any the client sent) and, with
`replace_late`, turns late answers to safe requests into `503`. The handler is not stopped:
it should read `remaining_ms` and give up itself.

api.name: overridden_method
api.sig: fn overridden_method(req: Request) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc:
The method a `POST` asks to be treated as, from `X-HTTP-Method-Override`,
`X-HTTP-Method` or `X-Method-Override`, or a form field `_method`; only `PUT`, `PATCH` and
`DELETE` are honoured, so an override can't turn a form into a safe or tracing request.

api.name: method_override
api.sig: fn method_override[e](next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e
api.doc: A wrapper that applies `overridden_method`, keeping the original in `x-original-method`.

api.name: internal_error
api.sig: fn internal_error[E](req: Request, err: E) -> Response ! log
api.doc:
The answer to a request whose handler raised `err`: a `500` problem that carries only the
request id, with `err` logged under that id, so internals never reach the client. Use it in the
handler lambda: `req => catch api(req) | e => middleware.internal_error(req, e)`. (Traps, such as
overflow or a failed contract, can't be caught; the server answers those with `500` itself.)

api.name: Ip
api.sig: pub type Ip = {v6: Bool, octets: List[Int]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: An IP address: 4 bytes for IPv4, 16 for IPv6.

api.name: Cidr
api.sig: pub type Cidr = {net: Ip, prefix: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A network: an address and a prefix length (0 to 32, or 0 to 128).

api.name: parse_ip
api.sig: fn parse_ip(s: Str) -> Opt[Ip]
api.doc:
The address `s`: dotted IPv4 (no leading zeros, which some parsers read as octal), or IPv6 with
optional `::` compression and a trailing dotted quad. Zones (`%eth0`) and brackets are not
accepted; `strip_brackets` first.

api.name: strip_brackets
api.sig: fn strip_brackets(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` without surrounding `[` and `]`.

api.name: unmap
api.sig: fn unmap(ip: Ip) -> Ip
api.doc: The address in IPv4 form when `ip` is an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`), else `ip`.

api.name: ip_text
api.sig: fn ip_text(ip: Ip) -> Str
api.doc:
The text of `ip`: dotted IPv4, or IPv6 as RFC 5952 recommends (lowercase hex, no leading zeros,
the longest run of two or more zero groups as `::`, IPv4-mapped addresses as `::ffff:a.b.c.d`).

api.name: parse_cidr
api.sig: fn parse_cidr(s: Str) -> Opt[Cidr]
api.doc:
The network `s`: `address/prefix`, or a bare address as a single host. Host bits below the
prefix are cleared.

api.name: cidr_contains
api.sig: fn cidr_contains(c: Cidr, ip: Ip) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `ip` is inside `c`. IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses match IPv4 networks.

api.name: private_networks
api.sig: fn private_networks() -> List[Cidr]

api.name: forwarded_for
api.sig: fn forwarded_for(req: Request) -> List[Opt[Ip]]
api.doc:
The client addresses a request passed through, oldest first: the `for=` parameters of
`Forwarded` (RFC 7239) when present, else `X-Forwarded-For`. Entries that are not addresses
(`unknown`, obfuscated names) are `none`.

api.name: client_ip
api.sig: fn client_ip(req: Request, trusted: List[Cidr]) -> Opt[Ip]
api.doc:
The client's address: walking the forwarding chain from the newest hop, the first address not
in `trusted` (your proxies). An entry that is not an address stops the walk with `none`, since
nothing before it can be trusted; a chain of only trusted proxies gives its oldest entry. The
server only sees headers, so this is only meaningful when every connection comes through those
proxies (listen on 127.0.0.1 or a private network).

api.name: IpRules
api.sig: pub type IpRules = {allow: List[Cidr], deny: List[Cidr], trusted: List[Cidr], allow_unknown: Bool} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
Who may call: addresses in `deny` are refused, then if `allow` is not empty only addresses in it
pass. `trusted` are the proxies whose forwarding headers are believed (see `client_ip`), and
`allow_unknown` says whether a request without a usable address passes.

api.name: ip_allowed
api.sig: fn ip_allowed(rules: IpRules, ip: Opt[Ip]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `rules` let `ip` (or an unknown address, `none`) through.

api.name: ip_filter
api.sig: fn ip_filter[e](rules: IpRules, next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e
api.doc: A wrapper that answers `403` to callers `rules` don't allow.

api.name: basic_credentials
api.sig: fn basic_credentials(req: Request) -> Opt[(Str, Str)]
api.doc:
The user id and password of an `Authorization: Basic` header (RFC 7617): base64 of UTF-8
`user:password`, split at the first colon. `none` when absent or malformed.

api.name: basic_challenge
api.sig: fn basic_challenge(realm: Str) -> (Str, Str)
api.doc: The `WWW-Authenticate` header that asks for Basic credentials in `realm`, in UTF-8.

api.name: secret_equal
api.sig: fn secret_equal(a: Str, b: Str) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether the secrets `a` and `b` are equal, in time that depends on neither their contents nor
their lengths (both are hashed first, then compared with `crypto.equal`).

api.name: basic_auth
api.sig: fn basic_auth[e](realm: Str, check: (Str, Str) -> Bool ! e, next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e
api.doc:
A wrapper that lets through requests whose Basic credentials `check` accepts and answers the
others with `401` and a challenge for `realm`. Compare passwords with `secret_equal`, or better
against a stored hash; Basic credentials are only safe over HTTPS.

api.name: request_host
api.sig: fn request_host(req: Request) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc:
The host `req` was sent to, from `Host`, lowercased, without the port and a trailing dot (IPv6
keeps its brackets); `none` when missing or not a valid host.

api.name: host_allowed
api.sig: fn host_allowed(patterns: List[Str], host: Str) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether `host` matches one of `patterns`: `*` matches any host, `.example.com` matches
`example.com` and its subdomains, anything else must be equal (case-insensitively).

api.name: allowed_hosts
api.sig: fn allowed_hosts[e](patterns: List[Str], next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e
api.doc:
A wrapper that answers `400` when the `Host` header is missing or not one of `patterns`, which
protects against DNS rebinding and host header injection into links and redirects.

api.name: forwarded_proto
api.sig: fn forwarded_proto(req: Request) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc:
The scheme the client used according to the proxy in front: `proto=` of the first `Forwarded`
element, else the first `X-Forwarded-Proto` value, lowercased. Only believe it behind a proxy
that sets it.

api.name: https_redirect
api.sig: fn https_redirect[e](next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e
api.doc:
A wrapper that redirects requests the proxy received over plain HTTP to HTTPS on the same host
and target: `301` for GET and HEAD, `308` for other methods so they are repeated as sent.
Requests without forwarding information are served as they are. Combine it with
`allowed_hosts`, since the redirect uses the `Host` header.

api.name: FetchPolicy
api.sig: pub type FetchPolicy = {allow_same_site: Bool, allow_paths: List[Str]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A Fetch Metadata resource isolation policy: same-origin requests, requests the user started
(`none`) and plain navigations pass; `allow_same_site` lets sibling subdomains through too, and
paths under `allow_paths` are open to everyone (for example public assets or OAuth callbacks).

api.name: fetch_allowed
api.sig: fn fetch_allowed(p: FetchPolicy, req: Request) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `p` lets `req` through. Browsers that send no `Sec-Fetch-Site` are allowed.

api.name: fetch_metadata
api.sig: fn fetch_metadata[e](p: FetchPolicy, next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e
api.doc:
A wrapper that answers `403` to requests `p` refuses, a defence against CSRF, XSSI and
cross-site leaks in browsers that send Fetch Metadata.

api.name: origin_of
api.sig: fn origin_of(url: Str) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc: The origin of a URL (`scheme://host[:port]`), or `none`.

api.name: OriginGuard
api.sig: pub type OriginGuard = {origins: List[Str] where _.all(valid_origin_pattern), allow_missing: Bool} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
OWASP's CSRF check with standard headers: requests with unsafe methods must come from one of
`origins` according to `Origin`, or `Referer` when `Origin` is missing. `allow_missing` lets
through requests that carry neither (some privacy tools strip both).

api.name: origin_ok
api.sig: fn origin_ok(g: OriginGuard, req: Request) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `g` lets `req` through: GET, HEAD and OPTIONS always pass; `Origin: null` never does.

api.name: origin_guard
api.sig: fn origin_guard[e](g: OriginGuard, next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e
api.doc: A wrapper that answers `403` to requests `origin_ok` refuses.
